summary: On macOS, background seats and exec tasks start under taskpolicy -b instead of a utility clamp, because nice and the utility class did not keep the daemon responsive under a build load

replay.detail: No stored history or replay change.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or coordination version change.

compatibility.detail: A seat or exec task launched on macOS after the daemon restarts runs under taskpolicy -b, so its resources are throttled below the utility class it started with in the previous build. Linux is unchanged. Running seats keep their priority until restarted. A seat that declares ST_SEAT_PRIORITY normal, or an install with seat_priority = "normal", keeps the daemon's priority.

downtime.detail: None. A daemon restart adopts live seats.

manual.detail: None. Set seat_priority = "normal" in config.toml, run st service restart and restart each seat to give seats the daemon's priority.

recovery.detail: Reverting restores the utility clamp; no state is written.
